summary: Show in Enclosing Folder is an action with a key. src/actions.rs: `ShowInEnclosingFolder` in `actions!`, bound to `secondary-enter` in the FILES context (Cmd+Return on macOS, Ctrl+Enter on Linux and Windows), inside the table between Open's keys and Quick Look's. src/finder/mod.rs: `enclosing_target()` is the one test all three surfaces use. It gives the path of the single selected entry when `shows_parent_column() && !in_trash()`, and gives nothing while a place's own items are still being read (`loading` outside a search). `show_in_enclosing_folder` calls `reveal_in_place` for that path and then `focus_files`, and is registered with the Finder root's handlers, so a menu reaches it from any focus. src/finder/menus.rs: the item menu offers the item when `enclosing_target()` is some and sends the action instead of calling `reveal_in_place` on a captured path, so the kit draws the key beside it. src/finder/toolbar.rs: the Actions menu has the row after Copy Path, shown when `shows_parent_column() && !in_trash()` and disabled when `enclosing_target()` is none. docs/manual.md: Searching, Recents, Opening files, the chooser's notes, the Item menu list, the Actions list and the file views' shortcut table. The Mac's menu bar does not have the item (see left_out).
changelog: Cmd+Return shows the selected item in its enclosing folder: the folder opens in the window with the item selected, and Back returns to where you were. It works on one selected item in search results, Recents, and results sent from Nushell, so a search can go from its words to a result's folder without the mouse: type, press Return to move into the results, then Cmd+Return. The item menu shows the shortcut beside Show in Enclosing Folder, and the toolbar's Actions menu has the command too in those lists. It does nothing in a folder or in the Trash.
behaviour_changes: The key. Cmd+Return (macOS) or Ctrl+Enter (Linux, Windows) in the file views, with exactly one item selected in search results, Recents, or results sent from Nushell: the item's folder opens in the same window, tab or pane with the item selected, a search ends, and the files have the keyboard. The key did nothing before. Seen in tests from a folder, from a search made in the Trash, in Recents, in sent results and in a file chooser; in my probes in the icon, list and gallery views, in a contents search, in the first pane of split view (the other pane didn't move), and on a folder among the results (its parent opens with it selected).

Back afterwards returns to the search, to Recents, or to the sent results. After Back to a search, the folder Back came from is the selected result when it is one of them, so a second Cmd+Return shows that folder in its parent.

Where the key does nothing: in a folder, in every view, including an item in a deeper pane of the column view; with none or several items selected; in the Trash when not searching; while a name is being edited (the name field takes it as Return, as before); in the search field (there it is Return: it moves into the results and selects the first one, so Cmd+Return twice from the field shows the top result in its folder).
File chooser (`--pick`): the key shows the result in its folder and chooses nothing; Return still chooses. The chooser's item menu still has Show in Enclosing Folder beside Choose.

Item menu: Show in Enclosing Folder shows its key (Ctrl+Enter in the Linux pictures; the kit draws Cmd+Return as the Mac's symbols there). It is offered where it was, one selected item in results, Recents or sent results, never in the Trash, and it now acts on what is selected when it is chosen, not on a path captured when the menu opened. With the menu open, the key itself performs the command and closes the menu.

Actions menu: a new row, Show in Enclosing Folder, between Copy Path and Show in Finder / File Manager, in search results, Recents and sent results only. It is dimmed unless exactly one item is selected (a click on it then leaves the menu open, like every dimmed row), and absent in folders and in the Trash. No key is drawn beside it; that menu draws none for Quick Look, Rename… or Move to Trash either.
Focus: chosen from the Actions menu while the search field has the keyboard, the search ends and the keyboard goes to the files, not to the emptied field.

Review fix. The command waits for a place's own items. When the window leaves a place, that place's items stay on screen until the next place has read its own, and Recents reads its own only once the index is ready (it waits up to a minute). In that time an item of the Trash that was still listed could be selected, and the key, the Actions row and the item menu's item opened the Trash's own storage folder as an ordinary folder. The item menu's could before this change too, by my reading of the click handler it had; the key I probed. Now the key does nothing then, the Actions row is dimmed and the item menu leaves the item out. A search's results are never the old place's, so the command works in them at once.

macOS `--term`: Ctrl+Enter is bound as well, by the existing alias rule for Cmd keys (derived from `bind_keys`, not run). On Unix the terminal build asks the terminal for the kitty keyboard protocol (src/term/tty/unix.rs), so a terminal that has it can tell Ctrl+Enter from Return; in one that hasn't, the key arrives as Return and opens the item.

Manual: Searching (the key, once the keyboard is in the results), Recents, Opening files (what the command is for and where it does nothing), Choosing files for scripts, the Item menu list, the Actions list, and a row in the file views' shortcut table.
left_out: The File menu item on the Mac's menu bar, which the plan had. GPUI's macOS menu code gives AppKit `key_to_native(keystroke.key())` as an item's key equivalent, and `key_to_native` (gpui-pre-macos 0.3.10 src/events.rs) has a character for Escape, Space, Backspace, the arrows and the function keys but none for "enter" or "tab": the item would get the word "enter" plus Command. Zed's pull request 28440 describes "the `e` of `escape`" drawn as a menu item's key in the same situation (I read the PR's description; GPUI has mapped Escape since). So File › Show in Enclosing Folder would most likely show Cmd+E, and macOS might also run it on Cmd+E. Not run on a Mac. The command is in the item menu, with its key, and in the Actions menu, and the key works. To add the item anyway: `MenuItem::action("Show in Enclosing Folder", ShowInEnclosingFolder)` after Get Info in `set_menus`, the action in the list of tests/controls.rs every_menu_bar_action_has_a_handler (the root handler is already there), and the manual's File row. A way to have the item with no key at all would be a second action that nothing is bound to; I did not add one.
Up on the first result moving to the search field: cut by the verifier.

`go_up` (Cmd+Up) showing the selected result, also in the form restricted to Recents and sent results: the verifier lists it under "cut from this change". Cmd+Up still does nothing in Recents and sent results.
Cmd+Return in the search field opening the top hit: left out by the brief. In the field the key is Return.
CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.
A key hint in the Actions menu. That menu looks keys up from the toolbar, where keys bound only in the file views don't apply, so none of them shows there (see Found, not fixed).

`cargo clippy --features term` was not run: src/term is untouched and nothing it calls changed its signature.

review_fixes: The Trash guard had a hole, closed in `enclosing_target()`: it returns nothing while `self.loading && !self.is_searching()`. `location_changed` keeps the rows of the place the window left until the new listing answers, and for Recents `load_listing` first waits for the index (`engine.wait_ready`, up to 60 s). With the Trash's rows still on screen under Recents, `in_trash()` is false and `shows_parent_column()` is true, so a Trash item selected then was shown "in its folder", which is the Trash's storage folder: the bug the verifier's `!in_trash()` was for. Probed before the fix: Trash, navigate to Recents, click the stale row, Cmd+Return, all before the listing arrived, and the location became Folder("…-trash"). `loading` is set only by a load for a new place (or the first one) and cleared by whichever load completes next; a search's rows are its own results (`drop_stale_results` empties them when it starts), hence the `!is_searching()`. Quiet reloads (Refresh, the index finishing, file operations) never set it, so the command is not held back in a list that is only being read again.

The item menu offers Show in Enclosing Folder by `finder.enclosing_target().is_some()` instead of its own `searching && single`, and the `searching` local is gone. The two were equal except while a place is being read, where the item would have been offered and done nothing. Now the key, the Actions row and the item menu use one test, as the verifier's plan asked.
Commit message: a paragraph on the above, after the one about the Trash.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code says. (1) The command opening the Trash's storage folder as an ordinary folder. `enclosing_target` refuses in the Trash, and the hole described under review_fixes is closed; both are pinned by tests that fail with that folder opened. A search made in the Trash is allowed on purpose: its results are indexed files where they are. (2) The key doing something where the user means something else. It is bound only in the FinderFiles context, where the key was unbound. A name being edited has the FinderFilesRenaming context and the kit's own Cmd+Return in its field (probed: the edit ends, nothing moves). The search field, the filter and pipeline fields, dialogs, the sidebar, the folder tree and Quick Look's window are outside that context. The kit binds Cmd/Ctrl+Return in its List, Input, Select and Combobox contexts; the file views use none of them (they are `uniform_list`s). On Linux and Windows, Ctrl+Enter is what Explorer and GNOME Files use for opening in a new window or tab; the verifier accepted that, and the key does nothing outside the lists above. A held key repeats harmlessly: after the first press the window is in a folder. (3) The item menu's command breaking, now that it is an action found through the focus instead of a click handler. The menu is drawn inside the Finder's own element, so the action reaches the root handler; seen in the list view (test), on an icon-view tile and in a chooser (probes), and from the Actions menu with the keyboard in the files and in the search field.

CHECK ONCE ON A MAC (nothing here could run there): Cmd+Return on one selected search result opens its folder with the item selected; the item menu shows the Return symbol with Cmd beside Show in Enclosing Folder; the menu bar has no such item (by decision, see left_out). macOS CI runs the_item_menu_shows_a_result_in_its_enclosing_folder with `kbd:cmd-enter`; if my reading of the kit is wrong it fails there.

For briefs still to come.
- context-menus-fit: `actions_menu` (src/finder/toolbar.rs) has a new `.when(finder.shows_parent_column() && !finder.in_trash(), ..)` row after Copy Path; if you bind `in_trash` as your plan says, use it there too. In `item_menu` (src/finder/menus.rs) the `searching` local is gone: the item is offered by `finder.enclosing_target().is_some()` and sends `ShowInEnclosingFolder`. Keep it in a chooser's item menu, it only navigates. tests/controls.rs the_actions_menu_shows_a_result_in_its_enclosing_folder and the_item_menu_shows_a_result_in_its_enclosing_folder pin where the item is and isn't, that the Actions row is dimmed with nothing selected, and the key hint in the item menu. For pictures: a right-click on a results row's Folder cell left that cell's tooltip drawn over the menu in one of mine; right-click the name cell.
- live-search-results (lane-d, at work): the item menu's item and the Actions row act on the selection as it is when they are chosen. If a quiet re-query drops the selected row while a menu is open, the command does nothing. `enclosing_target()` holds back while `self.loading && !self.is_searching()`; a quiet reload does not set `loading`, so reloading Recents quietly leaves the command alone. A reload of Recents that is not quiet would switch the key off until it answers.
- empty-state-messages, search-start-no-flash, and anyone who changes what the file area shows while a place is being read: tests/finder.rs cmd_return_leaves_an_item_of_the_trash_alone_while_the_next_place_is_read asserts that the Trash's item is still listed right after Cmd+Shift+F, before the listing answers. If you clear the rows on leaving a place (which would fix the first item under Found, not fixed for every command), that assertion fails by design: delete the test then. The `loading` check in `enclosing_target` can stay or go with it.
- column-pane-selection-by-path: after Cmd+Return in the column view the folder opens with nothing selected (probed: selected was empty, one pane), because `load_listing` selects in `self.selection`, which the panes don't read. Your step 4 covers it; cmd_return_shows_the_selected_result_in_its_folder would then hold in the column view too. cmd_return_does_nothing_in_a_folder_or_with_two_results_selected calls the public `select_in_column(0, 2, window, cx)`; keep that wrapper, as your plan does. The same goes for view-switch-keeps-selection.
- recent-searches: your plan records a search at the top of `reveal_in_place`; the key goes through `reveal_in_place`, so it is covered there with nothing to add in `show_in_enclosing_folder`.
- path-bar-no-io (src/finder/bars.rs): see the path bar item under Found, not fixed, if you are in `path_bar_target` anyway.
- split-active-pane, type-select-space, preview-page-keys (all add to src/actions.rs): `key("secondary-enter", ShowInEnclosingFolder, &files, cx)` sits between Open's last table key and Space -> QuickLook. The `files` predicate matches a one-pane window and split view alike. The handler is on each Finder's root; in split view only the pane with the keyboard moves (probed).
- select-all-perf: `enclosing_target()` clones the selection through `selected_entries()` once per key press and once per item menu or Actions menu opened, not per frame. `self.selection.len() == 1` would do without; a list the command works in is never drawn as columns.
- smart-folder-save-and-leaks, result-tie-break, restore-session-tabs, tab-drop-and-close, tab-bar-overflow, go-to-folder-keyboard, focus-lost-recovery: nothing to do. A Smart Folder is a search, and the key works in one (the implementer probed it).

Found, not fixed (there before, outside this brief).
- Rows of the place the window left stay on screen, and can be acted on, until the next place's listing answers, under the next place's rules. Probed: after going from the Trash to Recents, before the listing arrived, the Trash's item was still listed and selectable, and its right-click menu was the ordinary item menu (Open With, Rename…, Move to Trash) instead of the Trash's. By reading only, not probed: the other way round a folder's rows under the Trash get the Trash's menu, with Delete Immediately… one confirmation away. The time is a few milliseconds for a folder and up to a minute for Recents while the index is built. This change's command is guarded; the others are not. Clearing the rows (or drawing placeholders) when the place changes would fix it for all of them.
- A hidden file shown in its enclosing folder, with hidden files off: the folder opens and nothing is selected, because the file isn't listed. Probed with `.secret` among sent results. Search results leave hidden files out when they're off, so it takes sent results (or Recents, if it ever lists one) to see it.
- Column view: after any `reveal_in_place` the folder shows and the item is not selected in the pane (above, under column-pane-selection-by-path).
- Path bar in the Trash, found by the implementer and read by me in `path_bar_target`: it treats the Trash like Recents (`is_searching() || current_folder().is_none()`), so with an item selected the bar shows the item's path inside the Trash's storage folder, and a click on a crumb opens that folder as an ordinary one (the implementer's probe: location became Folder("…-trash")).
- The Actions menu draws no key beside commands whose keys are bound only in the file views: Quick Look, Rename…, Move to Trash, and now Show in Enclosing Folder (seen in the pictures, with the files focused too). A dropdown menu looks keys up from its button's place in the toolbar; only context menus also look from what had the focus. tooltip-shortcuts's record lists "Move to Trash ... in the Actions menu shows Cmd+Backspace" among the things to check on a Mac; on Linux that row has no key. On Linux and Windows this menu stands in for the menu bar, so the keys would be worth showing there. `PopupMenu::action_context` with the files' focus handle would do it, but it also changes where every row's action is sent and where the focus goes afterwards; not tried.
- macOS menu bar, by the same reading of `key_to_native` as in left_out, not run: Window › Show Next Tab and Show Previous Tab have `ctrl-tab` and `ctrl-shift-tab` as their first bindings, and there is no character for "tab" either, so they probably show Ctrl+T and Ctrl+Shift+T, and may act on those keys.
